name: Root Canal Therapy
teaser: Comfortable, effective treatment to save your tooth and relieve your pain.
overview: Root canal therapy is one of the most misunderstood dental procedures — and one of the most valuable. Rather than causing pain, a root canal relieves it. When the inner pulp of a tooth becomes infected or inflamed, root canal therapy removes the source of the problem and saves the tooth from extraction.

With modern techniques and local anesthesia, root canal therapy is far more comfortable than its reputation suggests. Most patients are relieved to find that the procedure feels similar to getting a standard filling — and the result is a healthy, preserved tooth.

whatToExpect.title: Diagnosis & Comfort
whatToExpect.body: We'll take X-rays to assess the extent of the infection and administer local anesthesia to ensure you're completely comfortable before we begin.

whatToExpect.title: Pulp Removal & Cleaning
whatToExpect.body: The infected pulp tissue is carefully removed from the inner canals of the tooth, which are then cleaned, shaped, and disinfected.

whatToExpect.title: Sealing & Restoration
whatToExpect.body: The canals are sealed with a biocompatible material, and a crown is typically placed to protect and restore the tooth's full function.

faqs.question: Is a root canal painful?
faqs.answer: No — the procedure is performed under local anesthesia and is designed to relieve pain, not cause it. Most patients are pleasantly surprised by how comfortable the experience is.

faqs.question: How do I know if I need a root canal?
faqs.answer: Common signs include severe toothache, prolonged sensitivity to hot or cold, darkening of the tooth, and swelling or tenderness in nearby gums. A dental exam and X-ray will confirm the diagnosis.

faqs.question: What happens after a root canal?
faqs.answer: You may experience mild soreness for a few days, which is normal and manageable with over-the-counter pain relievers. You'll return to have a crown placed to protect the treated tooth.

faqs.question: Can the tooth get infected again after a root canal?
faqs.answer: Root canal therapy has a high success rate. In rare cases, re-infection can occur, and retreatment may be needed. Proper follow-up care and a well-placed crown significantly reduce this risk.

faqs.question: Is it better to pull the tooth instead?
faqs.answer: Saving your natural tooth is almost always the preferred approach. Your natural tooth provides better biting function and helps maintain jaw bone density compared to extraction followed by a replacement option.
